WEEK: 2
DATE:
CLASS: SSS 1
SUBJECT: Literature in English
LESSON TITLE: African Prose: Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
SUBTITLE: Reading, Summary and Analysis of Chapter 1 - 5
PERIOD: 1st and 2nd
DURATION: 80 minutes
LEARNING OBJECTIVES: By the end of the lesson, the learners should be able to:
- highlight the major events in chapters 1- 5 of the novel.
- identify the characters and their roles in the chapters read.
- explain the significance of the events in the novel.
KEY VOCABULARY WORDS: Characters, chapter, war, post-war, trauma, etc.
RESOURCES/MATERIALS: A copy of Elma Shaw’s Redemption Road
REFERENCE BOOKS: Exam Focus Literature-in-English (2026-230), Essential Literature in English and Dictionary.
BUILDING BACKGROUND/CONNECTION TO PRIOR KNOWLEDGE: The students are asked these questions:
- What are the themes you can identify from the summary of the text?
- Mention some of the major characters in the text.
CONTENT:
Reading, Summary and Analysis of Chapter 1 - 5 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
Chapter one
Chapter one of the text details the commemoration of the death of the paternal grandmother of Bendu Lewis, Catherine May Tyler Lewis, nearly a decade after she died an undignified death in the Liberian civil war. Catherine’s remains were never recovered. Thus, the family opts to use a casket as a symbolic representation of their dead matriarch. Family and friends gather to commemorate her death, among whom are Bendu’s parents, Benjamin and Eva Lewis, who returned to Liberia for the memorial service and are now staying with Bendu’s older sister, Siatta, and her husband, Terrance Clarke, who had previously returned to Liberia. Bendu reminisces about the harrowing experience of fleeing with her sick grandmother during the war.  She had pushed Granny May in a wheelbarrow among the fleeing crowd. Some of the fleeing people urged her to abandon Granny May, but she refused. In her frantic efforts to get away from danger, she saw babies, old people, and children along the roadside. They had been abandoned by their people in the resulting chaotic run. In spite of her determination to protect her grandmother, the latter dies. In her grief, Bendu was unaware of about thirty rebel soldiers approaching. After experiencing some harsh treatment from the soldiers, she was forcefully dragged away by the soldiers. She lost consciousness and would regain consciousness later that day to find herself among the fighters who were setting up camps in the forest. Bendu is brought out of her reminiscence by a touch on her shoulder from a sympathizer. She looks around and sees familiar faces like Agnes, Tenneh, and Calvin. However, her grief intensifies due to her inability to narrate her traumatic experiences. She contemplates the potential reactions of her family and friends if they were aware of what she endured or the actions she took during her civil war ordeal.
Chapter Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
Chapter two introduces us to the character of Moses Varney as he heads towards the courthouse. He encounters a group of displaced teenage boys he knows near the courthouse parking lot who hail him. His driver attempts to drive the boys away, but Varney stops him and greets the boys and greets the boys. Among the boys, he recognizes Simeon and Alphonso, although he cannot recall the names of the others. Varney empathizes with the boys’ plight. He reflects on his own experiences of loss and displacement as a child. He vows to the boys that things will change and promises not to forget them before he walks away. Varney’s thoughts turn to the lack of justice in society as he enters the Temple of Justice. He recalls a time when justice was valued. He laments the current state of affairs, where people prioritize peace over justice. Varney concludes that true peace can only be achieved through equity for all and asserts that people must rise to liberate themselves.
Chapter Three Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
In chapter three, Bendu return to work after her grandmother’s memorial service. While on her journey, she reflects about the challenges the country has faced after the war. She soon arrives at her office, an NGO- Peace in Practice where she meets with her assistance, Agnes, who updates her. She is to hold a counselling session with some victims of the war. Agnes also relays Calvin’s message to Bendu. Calvin is a friend of Bendu’s late brother. He is also a major financial donor to the NGO and interested in having a relationship with Bendu.  Despite Agnes’ attempt to set Bendu up with Calvin, Bendu insists that the friendship remains platonic as she is still grieving her late fiancé, Jonah. Calvin visits later and has a conversation with Bendu. The conversation reveals that Bendu is trying hard to supress her wartime traumatic experiences.
Chapter Four Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
Chapter four is a continuation of chapter three. Bendu and Agnes are in the group counselling session with Rosetta, Josephine, and Tenneh, who are victims of the war. Rosetta is bitter after losing her husband to ethnic violence, Josephine is nurturing, and Tenneh struggles with depression. Bendu suggests therapy for Tenneh, who improves over time. The counselling group is assigned to write letters to those who dehumanised them during the war.
STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES: STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES: Review, Introduction, Conversational Approach, Think-pair-share and Small Groups
LESSON SEQUENCE AND DELIVERY
ACTIVITY 1(Review) The teacher reviews the last topic with the students by selecting some students to give a recap.
ACTIVITY 2: (Introduction) The teacher writes and shares the lesson title, learning objectives and key vocabulary words with the students.
ACTIVITY 3: (Conversational Approach) The students discuss the events in chapter 1 - 4 of the novel.
ACTIVITY 4: (Think -Pair- Share) Students, in pairs, share and evaluate different viewpoints on the roles of the characters.
ACTIVITY 5: (Small Groups) The students are put in small groups and asked to read chapter 5 of the text and analyze it.
ASSESSMENT (EVALUATION): The teacher goes through each group activity and corrects them where necessary.
WRAP UP/CONCLUSION: The teacher concludes the lesson by affirming or correcting the learners’ answers to the evaluation activity.
ASSIGNMENT: The students are to read and highlight the major events in chapters 6-10 of the text.
HOD/VP’S COMMENT AND ENDORSEMENT:
WEEK:                      3
DATE:
CLASS:          SS 1
SUBJECT:     Literature in English
LESSON TITLE: African prose: Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
SUBTITLE:
Reading, Summary and Analysis of Chapters 6-10 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
PERIOD:       1st and 2nd
DURATION: 80 minutes
LEARNING OBJECTIVES: By the end of the lesson, the learners should be able to:
a. summarize the major events in chapters 6-10.
b. identify the major characters in the chapters read and the roles each played.
c. explain the significance of the events in the chapters read.
KEY VOCABULARY WORDS: prosecute, security, escalate, revenge, bribe, justice, nightmare etc.
RESOURCES/MATERIALS: Copies of Redemption Road, charts displaying the main events n the text, etc.
REFERENCE BOOKS: Exam Focus Literature-in-English, Success Pen Literature in English by Abiodun J & Andrew O and dictionary.
BUILDING BACKGROUND/CONNECTION TO PRIOR KNOWLEDGE: The students are asked the following questions:
a. Briefly explain why Bendu is affected by her grandmother’s death.
b. What is the relationship between Bendu and Calvin?
CONTENT:
CHAPTER 6 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
CHAPTER 6: Bendu has resolved to prosecute Commander Cobra for what he did to her, and his other war crimes. Agnes tries to warn her that it might be impossible, but Bendu insists.The two women ride together in a chartered taxi to Peace in Practice. Before they open the office door, Agnes tells Bendu that she has informed Calvin and Siatta about her encounter with Cobra and they are already waiting to help. This does not go well with Bendu. Her sister, Siatta, becomes annoyed with Bendu’s response and expresses a desire to leave. Calvin intervenes to calm Siatta down and tells her that Bendu needs her family around her right now, even if she doesn’t want to admit it.
They convene in Bendu’s office where Calvin questions Bendu about Commander Cobra. Bendu admits to being too afraid of Cobra to gather any information about the details of his car. Calvin suggests arranging security for Bendu’s protection.
Bendu reveals that she intends to find Cobra and bring him to justice. Agnes doubts the feasibility of Bendu’s plan but Siatta supports her sister’s decision. Siatta wonders why Sierra Leoneans watch illiterate fighters as they rape and kill them for so many years. Agnes feels Siatta cannot understand as she never had a firsthand experience of the war because she ran away to America. Siatta claims that she would never have allowed anyone to take her dignity or life. But Agnes dismisses her with the claim that she “had absolutely no idea what it was like”. Calvin cuts into the argument to prevent it from escalating. He talks about how Bendu needs security at that point because they cannot tell what action Cobra might take if he discovers that Bendu is looking for him
Calvin promises to find Cobra but hopes that Cobra does not try anything stupid. He is motivated by his desire for revenge due to the trauma he suffers from watching his dear friend, Benji (Bendu’s brother) being killed by soldiers in 1980. He now sees in every soldier Benji’s killer. He is determined not to let history repeat itself. Agnes expresses concern over Calvin’s motivations and warns him to be careful in his quest for revenge.
CHAPTER 7 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
CHAPTER 7: The narrative shifts to Moses Varney, formerly Commander Cobra, as he visits the Judiciary chambers for the second time that week. He is welcomed by Judge Dagoseh. Varney describes the judge as corrupt but the only one willing to help his cause. Moses Varney sees Judge Dagoseh as a symbol of Liberia’s problems, especially with how he uses his position in the courthouse to collect bribes to liberate himself from poverty. Varney bribes the judge who in turn hands him a manilla envelope as he leaves. The encounter between the two characters is purely transactional, which is why Varney is annoyed by the judge’s claim of being glad to be part of the revolution even after receiving a bribe to that effect.
Another takeaway from this meeting between Varney and Dagoseh is that an impending revolution is implied that would lead to a change of government. The both characters are helping the revolution come to reality. They also have different perspectives about the coming revolution. For Dagoseh, it is a means for his “liberation from poverty” as evident in his collection of bribes to make it happen. For Varney, it is a means of “liberation of the people from tyranny”.
CHAPTER 8 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
CHAPTER 8: The search for Commander Cobra has begun. Calvin searches for Commander Cobra at hotels, bars, and nightclubs. Terrance (Siatta’s husband) despite his political connection, is unwilling to help search for Cobra. Bendu receives support from Siatta and Agnes as she resumes her normal activities. She, however, keeps having recurring nightmares, especially about her failed attempt to escape Duluma camp. She always wakes up before she has to face Cobra and Samson in the nightmare.
A week after her encounter with Cobra, Bendu and Siatta visit Calvin at his Congo Town home. Calvin, Bendu, and Siatta discuss various topics, including war stories and missing people. They talk particularly about a whole football team they used to sponsor who went missing. Siatta is optimistic that they will be found but Calvin says it is highly unlikely.
Calvin expresses his indifference to the war stories and says that he doesn’t feel any sympathy towards indigenous Liberians who suffered displacement and starvation during the war. There have always been ethnic tensions between indigenous Liberians and Americo-Liberians. Bendu tries to make Calvin see that the indigenous Liberians are victims of the war, especially the women and children. But Calvin dismisses her claim with the fact that women and children did the most ignominious things during the war in order to survive.
From the turn of their conversations, it is apparent that Calvin is still embittered by what the indigenous Liberians did to Americo-Liberians during the 1980 coup; how their grandparents and parents killed President Tolbert and his cabinet ministers; how they witch-hunted and tortured Americo-Liberians; and how, like in the case of Benji, they killed Americo-Liberians. While Bendu is shocked that Calvin could be so cold-hearted, Calvin remains unsympathetic towards whatever happened to the native people. He believes they deserved everything that came their way during the civil war. He sees it as them reaping what their ancestors did to the Congo people in 1980. However, Siatta thinks different and believes no individual should be punished for the sins of their ancestors.
Back in her house in the evening, Bendu tries to imbibe Siatta’s philosophy but realises that she is fooling herself, considering what she did and was done to her during the war which her family and friends are still unaware of.
CHAPTER 9 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
CHAPTER 9: Bendu has a nightmare recounting her experiences while she was held hostage at the Duluma camp. It was the morning after she was dragged away by the fighters, leaving her dead grandmother by the road side. Cobra (being high on marijuana) after cleaning his weapon, decides to test it on two unlucky men. Bendu and the other victims had been paralysed with fear. She meets Ma Musu who shares her tragic story of how her husband was killed, her two sons taken while she and her two daughters were brought Duluma camp. Bendu had revealed her background to Ma Musu. She narrates the events leading to her and her grandmother being caught up in the war. She tells of how she was forcefully brought to the camp.
Cobra had sent for and warned her against disrespecting the group. He also gives Samson (one of his henchmen) Bendu as a wife. Samson had successfully raped Bendu even though she tried to fight hard.
CHAPTER 10 Redemption Road by Elma Shaw
CHAPTER 10: Bendu wakes up and she is relieved to know that she had been dreaming all along. After eating breakfast, she goes to a supermarket nearby. She hears someone calling her name and is shocked to see Cobra who goes on to invite her for a drink. He tells her where he stays and gives her his contact information. Bendu frowns at Cobra for addressing her as Lieutenant TKO which was her war name. Cobra recounts the reason for the name Lieutenant Technical Knock-Out. She was given the name after she had punched Samson in the eye. Cobra is surprised that Bendu is still single. He reveals to Bendu that his current name is Moses Varney.
STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES: Review, Introduction, Conversational Approach, think-Pair-Share, Chunk and Chew, Small groups
LESSON SEQUENCE AND DELIVERY:
ACTIVITY 1 (Review): The teacher reviews the previous topic with the students.
ACTIVITY 2(Introduction): The teacher writes and shares the lesson title, learning objectives and key vocabulary words with the students.
ACTIVITY 3 (Conversational approach):  The teacher engages the students in a discussion around the questions under building background/connection to prior knowledge.
ACTIVITY 4 (Think-Pair-Share): The students are paired and allowed to identify the characters in the chapters read.
ACTIVITY 5 (Chunk and Chew): The teacher explains the significance of the chapters read and pauses intermittently for them to reflect on what is being explained.
ACTIVITY 6 (Small groups): Students, in small groups, share and evaluate different viewpoints of the chapters 6-9. Each group representative shares the lesson learnt from the plot of the novel.
ASSESSMENT (EVALUATION): The students are asked to summarise the meeting between Bendu and Cobra in chapter 10 of the text.
WRAP UP/CONCLUSION: The teacher concludes the lesson by affirming or correcting the learners’ answers to the evaluation questions.
ASSIGNMENT: The students are asked to read chapters 11-12 of Redemption Road and highlight the major events there.
